messages:
maria: heads-up — noticed a slow-but-steady rise in kv_residency_cardinality on prod over the last 36h, with matching small bumps in kv_evictions_total. hit rate looks flat-ish though. :thinking:

alex: can you paste the prom query you used? wondering if this is noise from a single noisy host or a cluster-wide pattern. :eyes:

maria: quick queries: 
```
sum by(cluster) (kv_residency_cardinality{env=\"prod\"})
kv_evictions_total{env=\"prod\"}
sum by(cluster) (rate(kv_evictions_total{env=\"prod\"}[5m]))
```
I pulled 36h window. grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/kv/kv-residency (private)

jon: I pushed a tiny flamegraph from the sampler traces — looks like page compaction work increased CPU a bit on hosts with long-context sessions. suspicion: more fragmentation means smaller reusable fragments -> higher cardinality reported. attaching perf-bot snapshot id: perf-246210-7

perf-bot: snapshot perf-246210-7 uploaded: https://perfbot.redwood/snapshots/perf-246210-7 (contains heap/fbprofiles + callstacks). top sample: kv_compact_pages (23%), kv_page_scan (12%), kv_mark_reuse (9%).

tess: if fragmentation is the issue, residency can climb even with good hit rate because pages are being split and not coalescing. we should add a 95p residency by model/host and a page-frag metric to dashboards. also want eviction age histogram to see if we're evicting young fragments more often.

alex: propose short action list:
- add panels: kv_residency_p95_by_model, kv_page_frag_count, kv_eviction_age_histogram
- enable 1h sampling of kv_fragment_reuse_rate (higher resolution for 48h)
- run a sampling job to collect hot sessions and KV page layouts (non-prod first)

maria: I can own dashboard updates. alex can you drop the prom queries for the new panels?

alex: sure, sample PromQLs: 
```
# p95 residency per model
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(kv_residency_seconds_bucket{env="prod"}[5m])) by (le, model))

# page fragmentation count
sum by(model) (kv_page_fragments_total{env="prod"})

# eviction age histogram (bucketed)
sum by(le) (rate(kv_eviction_age_seconds_bucket{env="prod"}[5m]))
```

jon: small caveat — that residency histogram relies on us instrumenting residency duration as a histogram. if not present we can approximate with percentiles over samples using kv_residency_seconds_summary, but resolution will be worse.

tess: for sampling job, here's a super-simple one-liner to run on a canary host (non-prod) that dumps page layouts: 
```
sudo /opt/redwood/bin/kv-sampler --duration 30m --output /tmp/kv-sample.json && gzip /tmp/kv-sample.json
```
use it with `scp` to your laptop and open with `scripts/kv-inspect`

maria: running that on canary now. will post results in ~40m. if we see a clear correlation with long sessions, plan is to tweak coalescer thresholds and re-run.

alex: also adding an alert idea: if kv_residency_cardinality grows >20% over baseline AND kv_evictions_total rate increases > 10% over 15m then page-frag-alert -> page-coalesce-canary.

perf-bot: scheduled: nightly batch profile (canary) at 03:00 UTC starting tonight. will upload to perf-archive and ping thread.

maria: thanks — if the canary shows fragmentation spike i'll file a quick RFC for coalescer tuning. otherwise we may need to iterate on sampler heuristics (batch-merge threshold).

jon: one more note — watch kernel selection/batching interplay. larger batches can increase KV working set during inference tails which might exacerbate fragmentation. keep generation batch-size on canary at current default.

maria: noted. tagging @tess for dashboard PR review when done. :thumbsup:

(tock)
